note: The custody/enforcement model E1 depends on. GitHub-side ruleset configuration is provisioned by the Eye in the genesis ceremony; the custody oracle (a later slice) drift-sweeps live state against this manifest. E1 code refuses to operate if its own closure digest drifts from the provisioned TRUSTED_CONTROLLER_DIGEST.

principals.merge_controller: the sole merger; controller-class code executed from a TRUSTED BASE checkout; holds no standing bypass of check-enforcing rulesets
principals.branch_publisher: the sole write-credential holder; separate job on a fresh runner; create-only pushes to hestia/fix-* only; no merge operation
principals.eye: bootstrap-only actor-restriction bypass for the two enumerated ceremonial merges; REMOVED at steady state

check_enforcing.applies_to: EVERYONE including the Eye and the controller
check_enforcing.controller_bypass: FORBIDDEN — the merge-controller must be ABSENT from the bypass list of every check-enforcing ruleset (checks are never bypassed)

bypass_actors_phased.transition: AFTER E1 lands, the Eye is REMOVED from bypass_actors; the Eye thereafter merges THROUGH the controller like every other principal

actor_restriction.github_actions_principal: in NEITHER list — a rogue workflow's write-scoped token is server-refused on any push/merge to main

drift_rules: The controller present in any check-enforcing ruleset's bypass list => custody-drift.
The Eye present in actor_restriction bypass_actors AFTER E1 lands => custody-drift (emergency Eye access is an explicit, visible, recorded admin ruleset change).
Any principal whose live scopes exceed the recorded bounds => custody-drift.
TRUSTED_CONTROLLER_DIGEST unset, or the running controller closure != it => controller-untrusted (fail-closed, controller refuses to operate).
